candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
candidate.educational_objective: Identify the two WHO hand-hygiene moments that occur before direct patient care: before patient contact and before clean/aseptic procedures.

options.A: Before touching a patient and before a clean or aseptic procedure
options.B: Only before touching the patient's chart
options.C: Only before leaving the unit for a break
options.D: Only before answering the telephone at the nurses' station

candidate.rationale: WHO's Five Moments approach includes two pre-care moments: before touching a patient and before a clean or aseptic procedure. The remaining moments are after body-fluid exposure risk, after touching a patient, and after touching patient surroundings.
candidate.source_claim_supported: WHO recommends hand hygiene before touching a patient and before clean/aseptic procedures, as two of the Five Moments.
candidate.source_document_title: Five Moments for Hand Hygiene / Key Resources on Hand Hygiene
candidate.source_locator: Your 5 Moments for Hand Hygiene > Moments 1 and 2
candidate.stem: According to the WHO Five Moments for Hand Hygiene, when should a nurse perform hand hygiene before care?
